Health counters and the last-failure code are updated before the optional reporter runs; reporter failure cannot propagate into diagnostic append or replace the recorded primary fact.
Any keyring retrieval failure leaves the index with no usable credential. The lazy verifier refuses with `INDEX_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` before Redis verification and model routing can stay up.
The deadline revokes the current link budget first. An OS shutdown failure still proceeds to socket close, the operation used to unblock a Windows read; later use needs a new verified generation.

A reset failure may leave a checked-out WATCH connection. The fallback disconnects, releases that connection to the pool and clears the pipeline so a later finalizer does not send after the request guard. Normal operation and surrounding failures keep their original outcomes if fallback cleanup succeeds.

Reconciliation is an opportunistic write. A typed refusal keeps the read bounded to the confirmed watermark; the subsequent read still takes its lock and checks link identity and deadlines before serving.

An unexpected request/storage fault invalidates cached folds and returns `MEMORY_STORAGE_ERROR` or the overriding deadline response. The finally releases the worker permit. Transport failures have separate connection invalidation.

With a failing keyring, neither the purge journal nor recovery key is composed and lazy service verification refuses `MEMORY_STORE_CREDENTIAL_MISSING`; an empty password is not used to admit storage operations.

An unexpected span-exporter exception becomes failure with the transient flag clear. The bounded retry loop still applies; exhausted permanent failures surface as `FAILED`, while exhausted transient failures surface as `QUEUED`. The tests explicitly expect one bounded retry for permanent failure.

The retry observer sanitizes the structured attempt record before logging. If construction or the log write fails, the callback returns without changing upstream attempt retry classification, terminal handling or success.

An unreadable registry leaves a missing provider as null or reduces a present provider to `unrecognized`. Route policy uses the original value for comparisons, and the fallback only affects bounded diagnostics.

Registry failure cannot leak an arbitrary model ID through the usage log. The fallback gives null for absent input or `unrecognized` for a present value; this calculation belongs to recording, outside the provider response checks.

After reserving an experimental admission, an unexpected exception or interrupt during the one transport call is treated as unknown usage and re-raised. The guard's unknown settlement prevents later calls from being treated as ordinary unbilled retries.

Conversion of `cost_usd` to Decimal maps failures to the usage contract's `ValueError`; separate checks reject non-finite or negative values. The enforced route catches invalid usage and does not report a successful valid-cost result.

If persistence sanitization raises, the response receives a fixed `internal gateway error`. Successful sanitizer results must also be a nonempty string before use; raw original errors are not the fallback.
The whole diagnostic formatting/write is secondary to sending the model reply. Any logger failure leaves `_send_json` reachable with the selected status and body.

Failure to write the bounded identity-mismatch event cannot preempt the 409 reply. Refusal has already set connection close and remains outside model or tool dispatch. The bounded request-body cleanup is a distinct arm.
A search adapter exception becomes a sanitized, correlated 502 `PROVIDER_FAILURE`. URL policy revalidation and usage construction happen only on a provider result.
A failure in the extract adapter becomes a sanitized, correlated 502; only a returned result proceeds to the requested-URL membership check and usage construction.
A package-provider exception becomes a sanitized, correlated 502. Returned citations are policy-checked in the separate successful provider path.
An advisory-provider exception returns the sanitized `PROVIDER_FAILURE` response and does not proceed to collect or authorize citation URLs.

After the bounded retry wrapper exits with an ordinary failure, the JSON adapter exports only the configured label through `ToolProviderError`. Body read, decoding and object-shape checks have already been performed before any success.

The byte adapter translates ordinary exceptions after the bounded outbound attempts into the safe labeled `ToolProviderError`; callers do not receive raw urllib errors or successful bytes from that arm.

The worker catches even control-flow exceptions to transfer the exact exception to the waiter. It always clears its thread-local watch and returns its permit; if the waiter times out, it separately abandons the attempt.
A worker-start failure returns the acquired capacity slot before re-raising. Once started, the worker owns the release in its own finally.

Every ordinary attempt failure is timed, classified and surfaced to the retry observer. Only recognized transient faults retry within count and dispatch-time budget. Terminal transient errors are wrapped and permanent errors are re-raised.
After connecting a socket, a failed attempt-registration step closes the new socket even on interruption and re-raises. It is never handed to the HTTP connection as an accepted watched socket.

A transport exception is classified as failed with an attributable HTTP status, otherwise uncertain, and re-raised. The finally submits the named physical attempt outcome, preserving billing uncertainty through interruption.
A keyring exception keeps capture in local observing mode and records the `credential_absent` reason. It never connects to the accounting store with fallback credentials or prevents Gateway startup.
The timer cancellation callback is best effort and independent of the report result. Failure to cancel does not drop the query's own deadline/statement timeout, so the callback is safe to contain.
Guard initialization failure releases the untransferred append handle and lock and re-raises the original failure.
